metadata.notes: Path H — Supply Chain: Trojanised Agent via Marketplace. Scenario: MaliciousAgentIntroduced (Layer 2 AI-Specific). Trojanised agent delivered through trusted vendor channels or AI marketplaces. The SolarWinds pattern adapted for the AI agent ecosystem. The trust dependency on the agent vendor/marketplace is the #10 generic vulnerability. Notation: #10 ||[dev][@Vendor→@Org]|| →[Δt=~2w] #7→[instant]#1 + [DRE: C, I]. Velocity: VC-1 (supply chain dwell), then VC-4 (activation and exploitation). Extended dwell time creates threat hunting opportunity (VC-1). After activation, exploitation is machine-speed. Supply chain validation and code signing are the primary cause-side controls. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Trojanised agent package delivered through trusted marketplace or vendor update channel. Generic vulnerability: third-party trust dependencies — organisation trusts the agent vendor/marketplace. Removing the trust link (not using the marketplace) would prevent this attack → confirms #10.
Backdoored agent activates and executes malicious functionality. Generic vulnerability: the software environment's designed capability to execute potentially untrusted foreign code.
Backdoor abuses legitimate system and agent functions for data collection and exfiltration. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in legitimate functions.
